text:
evan: weird latency spike in dedicated-usw3 around 01:42, p99 for multigpu workloads jumped ~3x. GPUs show high p2p traffic and NVLink saturating, co-tenants impacted. anyone seen NVLink storms before?
sophie: seeing nvlink_tx counters blow up on shelf s3 nodes r2n4-r2n6. quick log: 
```
2026-08-11T01:42:07Z gpu-metrics[r2n4]: nvlink_tx tenant=t-204 delta=18GB/s
2026-08-11T01:42:08Z p2p-proxy[proxy-3]: p2p_connect tenant=t-204 dst=node=r2n6 streams=12
2026-08-11T01:42:09Z scheduler[sch]: slab-frag tenant=t-205 reason=gpu-p2p-hotspot
```
reza: t-204 was recently migrated with a fractional carve that allowed cross-host p2p warmups. it's doing model-parallel shard stitching which is chatty. NVLink is local but PCIe P2P fallback might be hurting other nodes.
oncall-sre: i'm oncall. short mitigations: 1) throttle tenant t-204 inter-gpu p2p by limiting p2p streams, 2) disable cross-host gpu-direct for fractional promos, 3) if needed, live-migrate t-204 off the shelf. can ops run commands?
ops-automation: commands available: 
```bash
# limit p2p streams for tenant
rctl tenant update t-204 --gpu-p2p-streams=2 --note="temp-p2p-throttle"
# disable cross-host gpu-direct for promos
rctl config set prod gpu-network allow_crosshost_p2p=false
# emergency move
rctl allocation move --tenant t-204 --from=r2n4 --to=standby-pool --reason="nvlink-hotspot"
```
sophie: before moving, can we confirm p2p is the cause vs bad NVLink hw? quick query: 
```sql
SELECT node, sum(nvlink_tx) as tx FROM infra.gpu_nvm_stats WHERE time > now() - 10m GROUP BY node ORDER BY tx DESC LIMIT 6;
```
sophie: ran it  r2n4/r2n6 top, but r2n5 also shows elevated tx. all three host shards are pinned to t-204.
oncall-sre: apply the p2p-streams throttle and disable cross-host gpu-direct for promos. infra-bot: applying change now.
ops-automation: applied tenant throttle: gpu-p2p-streams=2 for t-204. applied gpu-network.allow_crosshost_p2p=false. infra-bot: config change recorded user=oncall-sre action=set gpu-network.allow_crosshost_p2p=false at=2026-08-11T01:46:12Z
ev an: monitoring p99 and nvlink. initial impact: nvlink_tx fell from 18GB/s to ~6GB/s within 40s. p99 improved from 720ms to ~240ms. co-tenants recovering.
reza: root cause theory: fractional promo allowed multi-host model-parallel warmups and the scheduler didn't detect aggregate NVLink/P2P pressure. warmup parallelism + high stream count created a full-bus storm that spilled into PCIe and caused slab fragmentation.
billing-bot: provisional egress-like charge flagged for org-204 due to inter-host transfer accounting; ops will reconcile. estimated extra intra-fabric transfer ~6TB -> ~$1.1k.
sophie: follow-ups: 1) add a scheduler check for aggregate nvlink/p2p usage per-shelf before allowing multi-host warms, 2) add per-tenant p2p stream default cap during promotions, 3) make allow_crosshost_p2p=false the default for fractional promos unless explicit opt-in. i'll file PRs.
oncall-sre: also request an automated soft-rollback for promotions that cause NVLink>threshold within 5m.
reza: medium-term: consider a cheap shelf-level P2P probe that estimates headroom by opening N ephemeral streams and measuring throughput, similar to TOR probe idea but for GPU fabric.
ev an: thanks. keeping watch for 15m. ping here if it recurs. :thumbsup:
